page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 2 physical cores at 1 thread per core, accompanied by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no bundled local storage and features zero graphics acceleration hardware.

Synthetic benchmarking reveals competitive single-core execution alongside predictable multi-core limitations inherent to a dual-core footprint. In single-core stress-ng testing, the server demonstrates strong performance with a score of 2692.58, while Geekbench single-core sits in the average band at 1502.0. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 26.13 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 11.31 GB/sec maintain stable throughput. However, aggregate multi-core metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core at 2729.0 and PassMark CPU at 4424.56, fall into lower performance bands compared across cloud fleets. Memory testing indicates constrained throughput, with uncached large-block reads registering at 35.65 GB/sec and writes at 22.54 GB/sec.

Application tests record 3.7 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Because it lacks attached local disks and provides modest total memory, it is not structured for heavy data pipelines, large in-memory caches, or demanding database operations. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without hyperthreading contention, making the t2d-standard-2 suitable for microservices, lightweight web servers, entry-level background workers, and low-concurrency utilities.
description: The Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is an entry-tier general-purpose instance offering 2 dedicated vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor paired with 8.0 GB of memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with single-threaded physical cores and 32 MB of L3 cache, the system maintains a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached persistence. Performance benchmarks show capable single-thread compute capabilities, achieving 2692.58 in stress-ng single-core tests, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth scale strictly within its dual-core footprint. Delivering 3.7 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 3.36 GB/sec in static web serving, this instance represents a predictable, cost-efficient resource tier for modest enterprise operations. It is best suited for deploying microservices, lightweight web servers, internal development environments, and low-intensity background utilities.
